passages.scripture: Therefore, holy brothers, who share in the heavenly calling, set your focus on Jesus, the apostle and high priest whom we confess.

lines.text: So you are holy brothers and sisters.
You share in the heavenly calling.
Focus your thoughts on Jesus.
Jesus is the apostle.
Jesus is also the high priest.
This is the Jesus we confess.

passages.scripture: He was faithful to the One who appointed Him, just as Moses was faithful in all God’s house.

lines.text: God appointed Jesus.
Jesus was faithful to God.
Moses also was faithful in all God's house — among all God's people.

passages.scripture: For Jesus has been counted worthy of greater glory than Moses, just as the builder of a house has greater honor than the house itself.

lines.text: A builder deserves greater honor than the house itself — and Jesus is the builder of God's house.
Therefore, Jesus is worthy of greater glory than Moses — who is part of God's house.

passages.scripture: And every house is built by someone, but God is the builder of everything.

lines.text: Every house is built by someone.
But God is the builder of everything — God created all things, including Moses, through Jesus.

passages.scripture: Now Moses was faithful as a servant in all God’s house, testifying to what would be spoken later.

lines.text: Moses was faithful as a servant in all God's house.
Moses testified to what God would later say through Jesus.

passages.scripture: But Christ is faithful as the Son over God’s house. And we are His house, if we hold firmly to our confidence and the hope of which we boast.

lines.text: But Christ is faithful as the Son over God's house.
And we are Christ's house.
This is true if we hold firmly to our confidence.
And if we never let go of the hope we celebrate.

passages.scripture: Therefore, as the Holy Spirit says: “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts, as you did in the rebellion, in the day of testing in the wilderness, where your fathers tested and tried Me, and for forty years saw My works.

lines.text: So listen to what the Holy Spirit says:
Today, if you hear God's voice, do not harden your hearts.
Long ago, your ancestors the Israelites rebelled against God.
That was the day of testing in the wilderness, when Moses led them.
For forty years the Israelites saw God's works — such as daily bread from heaven and a nightly pillar of fire.
And yet there in the wilderness the Israelites tested and tried God.

passages.scripture: Therefore I was angry with that generation, and I said, ‘Their hearts are always going astray, and they have not known My ways.’

lines.text: So God was angry with that generation.
God said, 'Their hearts always go astray.'
'They do not know My ways,' God said.

passages.scripture: So I swore on oath in My anger, ‘They shall never enter My rest.’ ”

lines.text: So God swore an oath in His anger.
'They will never enter My rest,' God declared.

passages.scripture: See to it, brothers, that none of you has a wicked heart of unbelief that turns away from the living God.

lines.text: So watch out, brothers and sisters.
Make sure none of you has a wicked heart of unbelief.
Such a heart turns away from the living God.

passages.scripture: But exhort one another daily, as long as it is called today, so that none of you may be hardened by sin’s deceitfulness.

lines.text: But encourage one another every day.
Do this as long as it is still called 'Today.'
Then none of your hearts will be hardened — grown stubborn and closed to God.
Sin hardens the heart by deceiving it.

passages.scripture: We have come to share in Christ if we hold firmly to the end the assurance we had at first.

lines.text: We have come to share in Christ.
This is true if we hold on to our original confidence.
We must stay firm all the way to the end.

passages.scripture: As it has been said: “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts, as you did in the rebellion.”

lines.text: As Scripture says:
Long ago, the Israelites rebelled against God.
Today, if you hear God's voice, do not harden your hearts as the Israelites did.

passages.scripture: For who were the ones who heard and rebelled? Were they not all those Moses led out of Egypt?

lines.text: Who heard God's voice and yet rebelled?
It was all the people Moses led out of Egypt.

passages.scripture: And with whom was God angry for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?

lines.text: And with whom was God angry for forty years?
God was angry with those who sinned.
Their dead bodies fell in the wilderness.

passages.scripture: And to whom did He swear that they would never enter His rest? Was it not to those who disobeyed?

lines.text: And to whom did God swear that they would never enter His rest?
It was to those who disobeyed.

passages.scripture: So we see that it was because of their unbelief that they were unable to enter.

lines.text: The Israelites did not believe.
So we see why the Israelites could not enter God's rest.
